arxiv-2010-12669.title: Position and Rotation Invariant Sign Language Recognition from 3D Kinect Data with Recurrent Neural Networks
arxiv-2010-12669.creator: Prasun Roy, Saumik Bhattacharya, Partha Pratim Roy, Umapada Pal
arxiv-2010-12669.description: Abstract Sign language is a gesture-based symbolic communication medium among speech and hearing impaired people. It also serves as a communication bridge between non-impaired and impaired populations. Unfortunately, in most situations, a non-impaired person is not well conversant in such symbolic languages restricting the natural information flow between these two categories.

arxiv-2106-15729.title: Probabilistic Control of Heterogeneous Swarms Subject to Graph Temporal Logic Specifications: A Decentralized and Scalable Approach Thanks: This material is based on work partly supported by the grants AFRL FA9550-19-1-0169 and DARPA D19AP00004. F. Djeumou is with the Department of Electrical and Co
arxiv-2106-15729.creator: Franck Djeumou, Zhe Xu, Murat Cubuktepe, Ufuk Topcu
arxiv-2106-15729.description: Abstract We develop a probabilistic control algorithm, GTLProCo , for swarms of agents with heterogeneous dynamics and objectives, subject to high-level task specifications. The resulting algorithm not only achieves decentralized control of the swarm but also significantly improves scalability over state-of-the-art existing algorithms.

arxiv-2112-08386.title: Non-parametric stellar LOSVD analysis
arxiv-2112-08386.creator: Damir Gasymov, Ivan Katkov
arxiv-2112-08386.description: Abstract Ill-posed inverse problems are common in astronomy, and their solutions are unstable with respect to noise in the data. Solutions of such problems are typically found using two classes of methods: parametrization and fitting the data against some predefined function or a solution with a non-parametrical function using regularization.

arxiv-2401-04725.title: Basic fractional nonlinear-wave models and solitons
arxiv-2401-04725.creator: Boris A. Malomed
arxiv-2401-04725.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Boris A. Malomed. This review article provides a concise summary of one- and two-dimensional models for the propagation of linear and nonlinear waves in fractional media. The basic models, which originate from the Laskin’s fractional quantum mechanics and more experimentally relevant setups emulating fractional diffraction in optics, are based on the Riesz definition of fractional derivatives, which are characterized by the respective Lévy indices. Basic species of one-dimensional solitons, produced by the fractional models which include cubic or quadratic nonlinear terms, are outlined too.

arxiv-2504-07746.description: Abstract We establish a uniform approximation of metric entropy by partition entropy using uniform partitions for 𝒞 1 , α {\cal C}^{1,\alpha} three-dimensional diffeomorphisms. arxiv-2511-18115.title: Muskie: Mu lti-view Ma sk ed I mag e Modeling for 3D Vision Pre-training
arxiv-2511-18115.creator: Wenyu Li, Sidun Liu, Peng Qiao, Yong DouTongrui HuNational University of Defense Technology
arxiv-2511-18115.description: Abstract We present Muskie, a native multi-view vision backbone designed for 3D vision tasks. Unlike existing models, which are frame-wise and exhibit limited multi-view consistency, Muskie is designed to process multiple views simultaneously and introduce multi-view consistency in pre-training stage. Muskie is trained to reconstruct heavily masked content in one view by finding and utilizing geometric correspondences from other views.

arxiv-2602-02951.title: Nüwa: Mending the Spatial Integrity Torn by VLM Token Pruning
arxiv-2602-02951.creator: Yihong Huang, Fei Ma, Yihua Shao, Jingcai Guo, Zitong Yu, Laizhong Cui, Qi Tian
arxiv-2602-02951.description: Abstract Vision token pruning has proven to be an effective acceleration technique for the efficient Vision Language Model (VLM). However, existing pruning methods demonstrate excellent performance preservation in visual question answering (VQA) and suffer substantial degradation on visual grounding (VG) tasks.

pmc-10560361.title: A nomogram to predict 28-day mortality in neonates with sepsis: a retrospective study based on the MIMIC-III database
pmc-10560361.creator: Yongzhou Liang, Liqing Zhao, Jihong Huang, Yurong Wu
pmc-10560361.description: BackgroundSepsis is the second-leading cause of death in neonates. We established a predictive nomogram to identify critically ill neonates early and reduce the time to treatment.MethodsIt is a retrospective case-control study based on the MIMIC-III database. The study population comprised 924 neonates diagnosed with sepsis.

pmc-11509866.title: Effects of Free or Immobilized Pediococcus acidilactici ORE5 on Corinthian Currants on Gut Microbiome of Streptozotocin-Induced Diabetic Rats
pmc-11509866.creator: Ioanna Prapa, Vasiliki Kompoura, Chrysoula Pavlatou, Grigorios Nelios, Gregoria Mitropoulou, Nikolaos Kostomitsopoulos, Stavros Plessas, Eugenia Bezirtzoglou, Vaios T Karathanos, Amalia E Yanni, Yiannis Kourkoutas, Harsharn Gill, Xiaoxi Xu, Yanfeng Tuo

pmc-11605405.title: Effect of watering before slaughter and the evisceration method on the quality characteristics of fattened goose liver
pmc-11605405.creator: Koppány L. Majzinger, Gábor Jónás, József Surányi, Ágnes Zimborán, Gabriella Kiskó, Andrea Taczman-Brückner, Annamária Barkó, László F. Friedrich
pmc-11605405.description: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of watering before slaughter and different evisceration methods on the quality characteristics of fattened goose liver. A total of randomly selected 60 male Greylag Landaise geese (Anser anser) were used to execute the experiment which had been force-fed during their growing period.

pmc-12514100.title: Comprehensive investigation identifies CPSF3 as a novel prognostic and oncogenic biomarker in bladder cancer
pmc-12514100.creator: Zhiyang Ma, Yining Hao, Wei He, Xin Xie, Danfeng Xu, Chenghe Wang
pmc-12514100.description: BackgroundBladder cancer (BC) remains a prevalent malignancy worldwide, with rising incidence rates each year. Despite progress in therapeutic strategies, many patients suffer recurrence or progression, emphasizing the urgent need for novel prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This research evaluated the prognostic relevance and functional role of Cleavage and Polyadenylation Specificity Factor 3 (CPSF3) in BC.

pmc-12649020.title: Systemic therapy followed by liver resection improved prognosis of hepatocellular carcinoma associated with macrovascular invasion
pmc-12649020.creator: Jinyu Zhang, Zirui Zhang, Qionglan Wu, Jinhua Zeng, Jingfeng Liu, Jianxing Zeng

This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of liver resection (LR) and the timing of systemic therapy in HCC with MaVI.MethodsThe SEER database included 106,613 HCC patients, 1,892 of whom had MaVI.

pmc-13226790.title: Swimming exercise training (SET) and MitoQ supplementation can mitigate the atrophy and inflammation process in skeletal muscles of male Wistar rats with spinal cord injury (SCI): NF-κB/MuRF-1/proteasome pathway
pmc-13226790.creator: Zahra Behroozi, Beydolah Shahouzehi, Daruosh Moflehi, Mahdiyeh Moradi, Fatemeh Rastegari Nasab Ravari, Mahdiye Lashkari-Zadeh, Maryam Hadadi, Mohammad Mojtaba Farazi, Soheil Aminizadeh
pmc-13226790.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In the present study, we investigated the effects of a rehabilitation period with MitoQ supplement and swimming exercise training (SET) on atrophy and the inflammation process in the skeletal muscles of male rats with spinal cord injury (SCI). In the present study, rats were assigned to five groups (n = 7): Sham, SCI, SCI + SET, SCI + MitoQ (250 μM), and SCI + SET + MitoQ. In the training groups, the rats underwent swimming training for 4 weeks, 5 days/week.

pmc-13613563.creator: Luiza F. A. de Paula, Lucas N. Perillo, Gianluigi Ottaviani, Flávio F. Carmo, Mandar N. Datar, Katherine C. Enebeli‐Ekwutoziam, Bruno Fogliani, Stephen D. pmc-13613563.description: Rock outcrops are geological formations that harbor a highly specialized biota adapted to harsh environmental conditions that differ from their surrounding landscapes. They are globally distributed, especially in old, highly weathered landscapes, and can function as habitat islands containing high levels of endemism and distinct evolutionary lineages.
